caption: A cat bats at its reflection in a shiny chrome kettle, and the reflected paw bats back from inside the metal.
expectation: The reflection moves at the same time, mirrored and warped by the curve of the kettle; the reflected paw cannot leave the surface.

caption: A boy looks over the side of a rowing boat into clear still water and sees his own face looking back, then the boat rocks and the face breaks apart.
expectation: The face is inverted and clear while the water is flat; it wavers and fragments as the boat rocks and returns when the water calms.

caption: A dancer's sequinned dress catches the stage lights, and dozens of small bright spots sweep across the walls as she turns.
expectation: The spots move when she moves and stop when she is still; they appear on the walls away from the lights.

caption: A man holds a glass tabletop at an angle to a window, and the garden outside appears faintly in the glass over the room behind it.
expectation: The reflected garden is dim and mirrored, shifts as the glass tilts, and disappears when the glass is laid flat away from the window.

caption: A woman walks along a hallway of polished steel panels, and a blurry reflection of her walks alongside in each panel.
expectation: Each panel shows a mirrored, slightly warped copy of her moving in step; the copies vanish at the gaps between panels.

caption: A woman puts a drinking straw into a glass of water, and the straw looks bent where it enters the water.
expectation: The part of the straw under water appears shifted relative to the part above, with the break exactly at the waterline; the straw itself stays straight when lifted out.

caption: A man stands waist-deep in a clear swimming pool, and his legs seen through the water look shorter and slightly bent at the surface.
expectation: The underwater part appears foreshortened and offset at the waterline; when he climbs out his legs look normal again.

caption: A child watches goldfish through the glass of an aquarium, and the fish swim clearly visible behind the glass.
expectation: The fish are visible through the glass and water at all times and stay inside the tank; the glass does not hide them or let them pass through.

caption: A woman looks out through a clear window at a garden, and a gardener walking past is seen through the glass.
expectation: The gardener is fully visible through the pane, undistorted, and moves continuously behind it; the glass does not make him vanish or appear inside.

caption: Rain streams down a window, and the trees outside seen through the wet glass wobble and blur where the water runs.
expectation: The view is distorted only along the running water and clear elsewhere; the distortion moves downward with the drops.

caption: A man holds a magnifying glass over a page of small print, and the letters under the lens appear much larger.
expectation: Only the letters seen through the lens are enlarged and they shift as the lens moves; the print outside the lens stays small.

caption: A woman puts on her reading glasses to look at a menu, and the text she is looking at through the lenses appears slightly larger and sharper than around the frames.
expectation: The change happens only in the area seen through the lenses and moves with the glasses; the menu itself does not change.

caption: A swimmer wearing goggles looks down at the pool floor, and the tiles below appear clear through the goggles and water.
expectation: The tiles are visible and their grid wavers slightly with the water surface; they do not disappear or move on their own.

caption: A glass of water is set in front of a card printed with a straight vertical line, and the line seen through the glass looks shifted and wider.
expectation: The line appears displaced only behind the water-filled part of the glass and returns to normal when the glass is moved away.

caption: A drop of water lands on a phone screen, and the tiny pixels under the drop appear magnified.
expectation: The enlarged pattern shows only within the drop and moves if the drop slides; the screen beyond the drop is unchanged.

caption: A man holds a clear ice cube up to a window, and the scene outside is visible through the ice, slightly blurred.
expectation: Light and shapes come through the cube; the view is distorted at its edges and where it has cracks; the cube does not block the view like a stone.

caption: A person stands behind a frosted glass door, and only a blurred silhouette of them is visible through it.
expectation: The blur moves as the person moves and sharpens as they come closer to the glass; details of the face never become clear through the frosting.

caption: A driver switches on the windshield wipers in heavy rain, and each sweep clears a sharp view of the road that blurs again as rain lands.
expectation: The view is clear immediately behind each wiper stroke and degrades between strokes; the rain does not clear itself.

caption: A child looks through a round fishbowl at her brother on the other side, and his face appears stretched and warped through the bowl.
expectation: The distortion appears only through the water-filled bowl and changes as either child moves; his face is normal when seen past the bowl's edge.

caption: A boy dips his hand into a clear pond, and the underwater part of his arm looks displaced from the part above the surface.
expectation: The break appears exactly at the waterline and disappears when the hand is lifted out; the arm is not actually bent.

caption: A diver looks up from under the water and sees the wavering shapes of people standing at the pool edge through the surface.
expectation: The people are visible but their outlines ripple with the surface; they steady when the water is calm.

caption: A shopper looks through a bakery's front window, and the cakes inside are clearly visible through the glass.
expectation: The cakes appear sharp and in place behind the glass; the reflection of the street is faint over them; nothing is hidden by the pane.

caption: A cook pours water into a clear jug standing in front of a patterned tile wall, and the pattern seen through the jug shifts as the water rises.
expectation: The pattern looks different behind the filled part than behind the empty part, with the boundary at the water level; the wall itself does not change.

caption: A person walks up to a clear glass door and pushes it open, having been fully visible through it as they approached.
expectation: They are seen through the glass the whole way; the door opens on its hinges when pushed and they walk through the opening, not through the glass.

caption: A woman looks at coins lying on the bottom of a clear fountain, and the coins appear to shimmer and shift as the surface ripples.
expectation: The coins are visible through the water and their apparent position wobbles with the ripples while they lie still; they do not actually move.

caption: A boy holds a clear plastic ruler over a line of text, and the text is readable through the ruler.
expectation: The letters are seen through the plastic with at most a slight shift at the ruler's edges; the ruler does not hide them.

caption: Sunlight passes through a clear glass of water on a table, and a bright patch of light appears on the table on the far side of the glass.
expectation: The bright patch lies on the side of the glass away from the sun and moves when the glass is moved; it disappears when the glass is taken away.

caption: A cook looks at a spoon standing in a clear glass jar of oil, and the spoon looks kinked where it enters the oil.
expectation: The kink appears at the surface of the oil and vanishes when the spoon is lifted out; the spoon is straight.

caption: A child presses her face to a window covered in raindrops, and the street outside appears as many tiny warped pictures within the drops.
expectation: Each drop shows a small distorted picture of the scene; the pictures move as the drops run down; the view between drops is normal.

caption: A snorkeler puts his mask underwater and the blurred rocks below suddenly come into sharp view through the mask.
expectation: The rocks are clear through the mask and look nearer and larger than they are; the view blurs again when the mask is lifted out.

caption: A man holds a clear glass jar full of water in front of his face, and his eyes seen through the jar look stretched wide.
expectation: The stretching appears only in the part of the face seen through the water and changes as the jar moves; his face is normal beside the jar.

caption: A woman looks at a garden through a pane of old wavy glass, and the plants seem to bend and shift as she moves her head.
expectation: The distortion changes with her viewpoint while the plants stay still; through a flat pane beside it the view is undistorted.

caption: A child holds a clear glass marble up to one eye and looks at a lamp, and the room appears tiny and warped inside the marble.
expectation: The small distorted image is inside the marble and moves as the child moves; the room around the marble is normal.

caption: A woman points through a bakery's glass counter at a pastry, and the assistant reaches in from the open back and lifts out the same pastry.
expectation: The pastry is clearly visible through the glass, the hand enters from behind rather than through the pane, and the pastry lifted is the one that was seen.

caption: A passenger looks out of a train window at a passing field, and the field is clearly visible through the glass as it slides past.
expectation: The view moves continuously past the window and stays visible; the glass does not turn opaque or freeze the scene.

caption: A woman drops a coin into a tall clear vase of water, and the coin appears to jump sideways as it passes through the surface.
expectation: The apparent shift happens at the waterline; underneath, the coin sinks straight to the bottom and is visible through the glass.

caption: A boy peers through a glass paperweight at a newspaper, and the letters under it look swollen and bent.
expectation: The distortion is confined to the area under the glass and shifts as the paperweight is slid; the letters outside it are normal.

caption: A woman looks at her feet standing in a clear rock pool, and they appear closer and larger than they feel.
expectation: The feet are visible through the water, enlarged and displaced at the surface; when she lifts a foot out it looks normal.

caption: A bathroom window is fogged after a shower, and as the glass dries the view of the yard outside sharpens patch by patch.
expectation: The view goes from blurred to clear where the moisture dries; it does not blur again while the glass is dry.

caption: A jeweller looks at a ring through a loupe held to her eye, and the ring's details appear greatly enlarged.
expectation: The enlargement applies only to what is seen through the loupe; the rest of the ring and the desk look normal size.

caption: A child looks at her hand through a glass of water, and her fingers appear fatter through the glass than beside it.
expectation: The widening shows only behind the water; the fingers seen past the glass edge are normal; the hand itself is unchanged.

caption: A diver in a clear sea looks up and sees the underside of a boat as a wavering dark shape through the surface.
expectation: The shape is visible but its edges ripple with the surface; it steadies as the water calms.

caption: A cook looks into a pot of clear water with vegetables at the bottom, and the pieces seem to shift and swim as the water is stirred.
expectation: The pieces on the bottom stay put while the moving water makes their images wobble; they look still again when the stirring stops.

caption: A woman holds a clear glass bottle of water sideways in front of a lit sign, and the letters seen through the bottle appear stretched.
expectation: The stretching happens only where the sign is seen through the water-filled bottle and changes as the bottle turns; the sign itself is unchanged.

caption: A child looks through a wet window and then wipes a patch dry with a sleeve, and the view through the patch becomes sharp.
expectation: The clear patch matches the wiped area and the view outside it stays blurred by the water; the outside scene does not change.

caption: A man wearing new glasses looks over the top of the frames and then through them, and the room appears sharper through the lenses than over them.
expectation: The difference appears exactly at the frame edges and moves with the glasses; the room itself does not change.

caption: A boy drops a stone into a clear stream and watches it sink, its image wavering with the current until it rests on the bed.
expectation: The stone is visible through the moving water and appears to waver while its actual path is a steady sink; it stays visible on the bottom.

caption: A lab worker holds a clear glass beaker of water in front of a ruled sheet, and the lines behind the beaker appear closer together and shifted.
expectation: The change is confined to the view through the water and vanishes when the beaker is emptied or moved aside.

caption: A woman looks at a shop display through a window streaked with rain, and the mannequins appear smeared where the water runs.
expectation: The smearing follows the water tracks and moves downward with them; the mannequins are clear through dry parts of the glass.

caption: A child holds a clear glass of water up to the light and sees the room through it flipped left-to-right and squeezed thin.
expectation: The flipped, narrowed image appears only through the water and shifts as the glass moves; the room seen around the glass is normal.

caption: Someone lowers a straight stick into a clear pond and the underwater part appears to angle away from the part above the surface.
expectation: The apparent bend is at the surface and its size changes with the stick's angle; the stick is straight when lifted out.

caption: A woman looks out through a car's side window at the passing city; the window fogs and the view goes blurry until she wipes a patch clear.
expectation: The blur grows with the fog and the view becomes sharp only where she wipes; the city outside does not change.

caption: A child places a glass of water on a line drawn on a piece of paper, and the line under the glass appears broken from the line outside it.
expectation: The apparent break is at the glass edges and the line returns to one straight line when the glass is lifted.

caption: A man holds a pair of binoculars to his eyes and looks at a distant bird, and the bird appears large and close through the lenses.
expectation: The enlarged view appears only through the eyepieces and follows where the binoculars point; the bird seen without them is small.

caption: A cook lifts a clear lid from a pot, and the food that was visible through the lid is seen the same underneath.
expectation: The food seen through the lid matches what is there when the lid comes off; the lid did not hide or change it.

caption: A woman enters a dark living room and flips the wall switch, and the ceiling light comes on and the room is lit.
expectation: The room goes from dark to lit at the instant of the switch and stays lit; the brightness comes from the ceiling fixture and casts shadows downward.

caption: A man turns off the bedside lamp, and the bedroom goes dark except for the faint glow from the window.
expectation: The lamp's light and the shadows it cast vanish at once; the room does not stay lit after the lamp is off.

caption: A child points a flashlight at a dark wall and sweeps it across, and the bright spot slides along the wall with the movement of her hand.
expectation: The spot moves in the direction the flashlight turns and stays lit only where the beam points; it does not remain on the wall after the beam moves.

caption: A group sits around a single candle in a dark room, and the candle lights up the faces nearest to it while the far wall stays dark.
expectation: The faces closest to the flame are brightest, brightness falls off with distance, and the light flickers with the flame.

caption: A car turns onto a dark country road and switches on its headlights, and two beams light up the road ahead.
expectation: The lit area appears in front of the car the instant the lights come on and moves with the car; the road behind stays dark.

caption: A child hides under a blanket with a flashlight, and the blanket glows from inside where the light is.
expectation: The glow is brightest where the flashlight is nearest the cloth and moves as the child moves it; it stops when the light is switched off.

caption: A lighthouse beam sweeps around in the night, lighting up the sea and cliffs in turn as it passes.
expectation: Each part of the scene brightens only as the beam crosses it and darkens again after; the beam rotates steadily.

caption: A spotlight follows an actor as she walks across a dark stage, and the circle of light moves with her.
expectation: The lit circle stays centred on the actor and the rest of the stage stays dark; her shadow falls on the floor away from the spotlight.

caption: A man opens a refrigerator door in a dark kitchen, and light from inside the fridge spills out across the floor.
expectation: The light appears as the door opens, widens with the door, and lights the floor and his front; it disappears when the door closes.

caption: A woman looks at her phone in a dark room, and the screen lights her face from below.
expectation: Her face is lit on the side facing the screen and the glow changes when the screen's picture changes; it goes dark when the phone is locked.

caption: A man moves a desk lamp closer to the book he is reading, and the page becomes brighter.
expectation: The page brightens as the lamp approaches and dims when it is moved back; the lamp's shadow of the book's edge shifts accordingly.

caption: A woman turns a dimmer knob slowly, and the ceiling lights fade from bright to a dim glow.
expectation: The brightness follows the knob smoothly, down when turned down and up when turned up; it does not jump or change on its own.

caption: A cloud covers the sun over a picnic, and the whole scene dims, then brightens again when the cloud passes.
expectation: The dimming and brightening are gradual and affect everything at once; sharp shadows soften while the cloud is in front of the sun.

caption: A man pulls open heavy curtains in a dim bedroom, and daylight floods in and brightens the room.
expectation: The light enters through the widening gap and the room brightens as the curtains open; the brightest part is nearest the window.

caption: A hiker strikes a match in a dark cave, and the flame lights the rock walls around her for a moment.
expectation: The nearby walls brighten with a warm flicker and the light fades as the match burns down; the far reaches stay dark.

caption: A camper walks through a dark campsite carrying a lantern, and the pool of light moves along the ground with him.
expectation: The lit area travels with the lantern and the tents brighten as he passes and darken behind him; his shadow falls away from the lantern.

caption: A caver wearing a headlamp turns his head from side to side, and the beam sweeps across the cave walls with each turn.
expectation: The lit patch moves exactly with his head and the wall he looks away from goes dark; the light is brightest where the beam is centred.

caption: A presenter uses a laser pointer on a projection screen, and the red dot moves across the slide as she moves her hand.
expectation: The dot appears only when the button is pressed, moves with her hand, and disappears when she releases it; it does not linger.

caption: Dusk falls on a residential street, and the streetlights flicker on one after another along the road.
expectation: Each lamp lights the pavement beneath it with a pool of light; the pools appear only under lamps that are on.

caption: A photographer takes a picture with a flash in a dim hall, and the whole room is lit for an instant.
expectation: The flash is a single brief burst that lights everything facing the camera and is gone; the room returns to dim immediately.

caption: A driver enters a tunnel on a sunny day, and the inside of the car dims until the overhead tunnel lights take over.
expectation: The light in the car drops as the tunnel entrance passes overhead and takes on the tunnel lamps' colour; it brightens again at the exit.

caption: A boy points a flashlight at the wall and then swings it up to the ceiling, and the lit spot leaves the wall and appears on the ceiling.
expectation: The spot travels up the wall and onto the ceiling continuously with the beam; the wall goes dark once the beam has left it.

caption: A television is switched on in a dark room, and the walls and the faces of the viewers glow with the changing light from the screen.
expectation: The glow on the room changes with the picture and comes from the screen's direction; it stops when the TV is switched off.

caption: A man cups his hand over the front of a flashlight, and the beam is blocked and the room goes dark.
expectation: The light disappears the instant the hand covers the lens and his fingers glow red at the edges; the beam returns when the hand is removed.

caption: A door to a lit hallway is opened into a dark room, and a wedge of light spreads across the floor as the door swings.
expectation: The lit wedge widens with the door and narrows as it closes; the door's shadow edge moves with it.

caption: Two people stand at different distances from a single lamp in a dark room, and the one nearer the lamp is lit far more brightly than the one farther away.
expectation: Brightness falls off with distance from the lamp; when the far person walks toward it she brightens.

caption: A cyclist switches on a bicycle headlight at night, and a cone of light appears on the path ahead.
expectation: The lit patch appears in front of the bike when the light is switched on and moves with the bike; the path behind stays dark.

caption: A person carries a lit candle down a dark staircase, and the light on the walls travels with the candle.
expectation: The walls are brightest near the flame and darken behind as the candle moves on; the light flickers with the flame.

caption: A power cut hits a house at night, and every light goes out at once, leaving the rooms dark.
expectation: All lamps go dark at the same instant and stay dark; only outside light through windows remains.

caption: A man strikes a lighter in a dark garage and holds it up, and the small flame lights his hand and face and the nearby tools.
expectation: Only things near the flame are visible, lit from the flame's direction; the light flickers and goes out when the lighter closes.

caption: A child switches on a night light in a dark bedroom, and a soft glow lights the corner around it.
expectation: The glow is strongest on the wall next to the night light and fades across the room; the far side stays dim.

caption: A car's interior light comes on when the door is opened at night, and it goes off again after the door is shut.
expectation: The cabin brightens when the door opens and darkens after it closes; the light comes from the ceiling fixture.

caption: A woman opens the door of a lit oven in a dim kitchen, and the food inside is lit by the oven lamp.
expectation: The inside of the oven is bright and light spills a little onto the floor; the light comes from the bulb inside, not from the food.

caption: A cinema's house lights dim before the film starts, and the audience fades from view until only the screen glows.
expectation: The dimming is gradual, the seats go dark, and the screen's light on the front rows changes with the picture.

caption: A worker turns on a floodlight over a building site at dusk, and the yard is lit while the area behind the light stays dark.
expectation: The lit area is in front of the lamp and objects there cast long shadows away from it; the ground behind the lamp is not lit.

caption: A man lights a row of paper lanterns hanging in a garden, and each lantern glows as its candle is lit.
expectation: A lantern glows only after its candle is lit and lights the leaves nearest to it; unlit lanterns stay dark.

caption: A boy shines a flashlight through his cupped fingers, and his fingers glow red where the light passes through them.
expectation: The glow appears where the flesh is thin and disappears when the flashlight is turned off; the light beyond the hand is dim.

caption: A stage's lights are turned up gradually, and the dark set becomes visible piece by piece as the brightness rises.
expectation: The scene brightens smoothly with no jumps; shadows appear away from the lamps; it does not brighten before the lights come up.

caption: A woman walks from a bright sunlit street into a dim shop, and the doorway behind her stands out as a bright rectangle.
expectation: The interior is dim relative to the doorway, the floor near the door is lit, and it grows darker deeper into the shop.

caption: A firework bursts high in the night sky, and for a moment the upturned faces of the crowd below are lit.
expectation: The faces brighten at the burst and dim as it fades; the light comes from above; the ground is lit only briefly.

caption: A person turns a desk lamp to point at the wall, and the wall brightens while the desk beneath it goes dim.
expectation: The lit area moves with the lamp head; whatever the lamp is aimed at is brightest and what it turns away from darkens.

caption: A car drives past a house at night, and its headlights sweep across the front windows, lighting the curtains for a moment.
expectation: The light moves along the wall in the direction the car travels and is gone once the car has passed; the wall does not stay lit.

caption: A student switches on a lamp with a coloured shade, and the shade glows while the desk below is lit through its open bottom.
expectation: The shade glows evenly with the bulb inside and the brightest spot is directly beneath the shade; the light stops when the lamp is off.

caption: A man walks through an office with motion-sensor lights, and the ceiling panels switch on ahead of him and go off behind him.
expectation: Each panel lights as he approaches and its patch of floor brightens; panels far behind him go dark after a delay.

caption: A woman blows out the last candle at a dinner table, and the faces around the table fall into darkness.
expectation: The warm light on the faces disappears with the flame; the room stays dark afterwards.

caption: A man switches on a torch app on his phone and holds it up in a dark basement, and the beam lights the floor and shelves in front of him.
expectation: The lit area is where the phone points and moves with it; the space behind him remains dark.

caption: A garage door rolls up in the morning, and daylight moves across the floor from the front to the back as the door opens.
expectation: The lit region on the floor grows inward as the door rises; the rear of the garage brightens last.

caption: A diver switches on an underwater torch in murky water, and a cone of lit particles appears in front of it.
expectation: The lit cone points where the torch points, fades with distance, and moves with the diver's hand; the water behind stays dark.

caption: A woman turns on a string of fairy lights along a fence, and small pools of light appear under each bulb.
expectation: Every bulb on the string lights together and each lights the fence close to it; nothing between bulbs is bright.

caption: A camper turns a lantern down to its lowest setting, and the tent interior darkens until only the nearest faces are visible.
expectation: The brightness falls smoothly as the knob is turned; the farthest corners darken first; it does not brighten on its own.

caption: A painter squeezes yellow and blue paint side by side on a palette and stirs them together with a brush, and the mixture turns green.
expectation: Green appears where the two colours meet and spreads as the stirring continues until no pure yellow or blue is left; the mixture does not separate back.

caption: A child adds a drop of red food colouring to a glass of white icing and stirs, and the icing turns pink.
expectation: Streaks of red spread through the white and blend to an even pink; the colour does not come out again.

caption: A red stage light is switched on over a dancer in a white dress, and the dress turns red under the light.
expectation: The dress looks red only while the red light is on and where the light reaches; it looks white again when the light changes.

caption: Sunlight shines through a stained-glass window, and coloured patches of light lie across the church floor.
expectation: Each patch has the colour of the glass it came through and lies on the floor away from the window; the patches fade when a cloud covers the sun.

caption: A boy tapes a piece of blue cellophane over a flashlight, and the beam on the wall turns blue.
expectation: The lit spot on the wall changes to blue as soon as the film covers the lens and goes white again when it is removed.

caption: A gardener sprays a fine mist from a hose with the sun behind her, and a small rainbow appears in the spray.
expectation: The rainbow appears within the mist while the spray runs and disappears when the water is turned off; it is not on the ground or in the dry air.

caption: A ray of sunlight hits a glass prism on a windowsill, and a band of rainbow colours appears on the wall.
expectation: The coloured band appears on the side away from the sun and moves when the prism is turned; it disappears when the prism is taken away.

caption: A crystal chandelier catches afternoon sunlight, and little flecks of rainbow light scatter across the walls and ceiling.
expectation: The flecks appear only while the sun hits the crystals and move when the chandelier sways; they vanish when the sun is blocked.

caption: A woman drips blue ink into a glass of clear water, and the blue spreads in swirls until the water is evenly tinted.
expectation: The colour spreads outward and downward from the drop and gets paler as it spreads; it does not gather back into a drop.

caption: A cook stirs a spoonful of turmeric into a pot of white rice, and the rice turns yellow where the spice is mixed in.
expectation: Yellow spreads from the spoon through the rice as it is stirred, and streaks even out; the rice does not return to white.

caption: A child mixes red and white paint on a paper plate with a finger, and the swirl turns pink.
expectation: Pink appears where the finger blends the two and the streaks become uniform with more mixing; the colours do not separate.

caption: A DJ switches a party light from white to green, and the white walls of the room turn green.
expectation: The walls change colour with the light and at the same instant; things in the light's shadow stay unchanged.

caption: A car brakes on a rain-wet street at night, and red light from its brake lights spreads over the wet road behind it.
expectation: The red glow appears on the road when the lights come on and disappears when they go off; it lies behind the car, not in front.

caption: Morning sun shines through red curtains, and the white bedroom walls take on a red tint.
expectation: The tint is strongest where the light through the curtain falls and disappears when the curtains are opened; the walls are white in ordinary light.

caption: A woman changes a smart bulb from white to purple with her phone, and the room's white ceiling turns purple.
expectation: The ceiling colour changes with the bulb and returns to white when the bulb does; surfaces the bulb does not reach are unchanged.

caption: A boy holds a piece of red plastic in front of his eyes, and everything he looks at through it looks red.
expectation: Only the view through the plastic is tinted; the scene beyond its edges is normal; the tint vanishes when the plastic is lowered.

caption: A child drops a purple bath bomb into a tub of clear water, and the colour billows out and turns the whole bath purple.
expectation: The colour spreads from the bath bomb as it fizzes, thinning as it goes, until the water is evenly coloured; the water does not clear again.

caption: Snow falls under an orange streetlamp, and the snow on the ground beneath the lamp looks orange while the snow farther away looks white.
expectation: The tint is strongest directly under the lamp and fades with distance; snow outside the lamp's reach stays white.

caption: A painter dabs blue paint onto a wet patch of yellow watercolour, and the colours bleed into each other making green where they meet.
expectation: The green forms along the boundary and widens as the paint spreads; the pure colours remain farther from the join.

caption: Sunlight passes through a glass of red wine on a white tablecloth, and a red patch of light appears on the cloth beside the glass.
expectation: The red patch lies on the side away from the sun and moves when the glass moves; it disappears when the glass is lifted.

caption: A cook pours a little green food colouring into a bowl of white cake batter and stirs, and the batter turns pale green.
expectation: Green streaks spread with each stir and even out; the batter does not turn back to white.

caption: A lighting technician crosses a red and a blue spotlight on a white backdrop, and the area where they overlap glows purple.
expectation: The overlap is a different colour from either beam alone and disappears when one light is turned off; the single-colour areas stay red and blue.

caption: A child looks at a white lamp through a jar of yellow juice, and the lamp looks yellow through the jar.
expectation: The lamp is tinted only where seen through the juice; beside the jar it looks white.

caption: A man wearing yellow-tinted sunglasses looks at a white wall, and the wall looks yellow to him through the lenses.
expectation: The tint appears only through the lenses; when he lifts the glasses the wall is white.

caption: A girl swirls a brush loaded with red paint through a jar of clean water, and the water turns pink and cloudy.
expectation: Colour streams off the brush and spreads through the jar, getting more even with each swirl; the water does not clear.

caption: A hairdresser squeezes two shades of hair dye into a bowl and whisks them together, and the mixture becomes one uniform colour.
expectation: Streaks of the two shades blend with each stroke until the bowl is a single even colour; the shades do not separate again.

caption: A theatre spotlight with a blue filter is aimed at a white piano, and the piano turns blue under the beam.
expectation: The piano looks blue where the beam hits and white where it does not; it returns to white when the filter is removed.

caption: Sunlight passes through a blue glass bottle on a windowsill, and a blue patch of light lies on the counter beside it.
expectation: The patch is on the side away from the sun and matches the bottle's colour; it moves when the bottle is moved.

caption: A child drips yellow and red watercolour onto a wet sheet of paper, and where they run together an orange band forms.
expectation: The orange forms only where the two colours meet and spreads as they bleed; the pure colours remain at the edges.

caption: A woman holds a green glass up to the light and looks at a white wall through it, and the wall looks green.
expectation: The tint is only in the view through the glass; the wall around it is white and returns to white when the glass is lowered.

caption: A fountain's spray in a park is lit at night by coloured lamps, and the falling water glows in the lamps' colours.
expectation: The water takes the colour of whatever lamp lights it and changes when the lamps change; unlit water is dark.

caption: A cook drops a spoonful of beet juice into a bowl of white yogurt and folds it in, and the yogurt turns pink with darker streaks that fade as it is mixed.
expectation: The pink spreads from the juice as the spoon moves and evens out with more folding; the yogurt does not become white again.

caption: Sunlight through a sprinkler's fan of water forms a rainbow that shifts as the sprinkler swings.
expectation: The rainbow is inside the spray and moves with it; it disappears when the sprinkler stops or the sun is covered.

caption: A stage floods with yellow light, and the actors' white costumes all look yellow at once.
expectation: Every lit white surface changes together to yellow and back when the light changes; shadowed folds stay darker.

caption: A child adds blue drops to a glass of yellow lemonade and swirls it, and the drink turns green.
expectation: Green appears where the blue meets the yellow and spreads until the whole glass is green; the drink does not separate back into yellow and blue.

caption: A tattoo shop's red neon sign shines on the wet white van parked outside, and the van's side glows pink-red.
expectation: The van is tinted where the sign's light reaches and white elsewhere; the tint goes when the sign is switched off.

caption: A painter rolls white paint over a patch of wet red paint on a wall, and the roller leaves a pink streak where they blend.
expectation: Pink appears only along the roller's path through the red; the untouched red stays red and the pink does not turn white again.

caption: Sunset light through a window falls on a white cat, and its fur takes on an orange glow.
expectation: The fur looks orange only on the side facing the window and while the sunset light lasts; it is white in ordinary light.

caption: A red plastic cup is placed upside down over a phone's white flashlight, and the cup glows red and throws a red circle onto the ceiling.
expectation: The glow and the circle appear when the cup covers the light and are the cup's colour; they vanish when the cup is lifted or the light is switched off.

caption: A car wash's foaming brushes turn from white to blue when the blue soap is sprayed on, and rinse back to white under clear water.
expectation: The colour spreads with the soap and washes out with the rinse water running downward; the brushes do not turn blue before the soap arrives.

caption: A red laser pointer's dot lands on a white wall, and when it moves onto a green plant the dot becomes hard to see.
expectation: The dot is bright red on the white wall and dim on the green leaves; it stays red wherever it lands and moves with the hand.

caption: A woman drapes a sheer red scarf over a white lamp, and the room's light turns warm red.
expectation: The room's light changes as the scarf covers the lamp and returns to white when it is lifted; the scarf glows from within.

caption: A child dips a white paper towel corner into a cup of blue dye, and the blue creeps up the towel.
expectation: The colour climbs from the wet corner upward and stops advancing when the towel is lifted out; it does not spread from the dry end.

caption: A jeweller holds a clear-cut crystal pendant in sunlight and turns it, and coloured sparkles dance across the shop's ceiling.
expectation: The sparkles move as the pendant turns and disappear when it is put down or the sun goes in.

caption: A bartender pours grenadine into a glass of orange juice, and the red sinks and spreads through the bottom of the glass while the top stays orange.
expectation: The red drops through the juice and gathers low, blending into a red-orange band; it does not float on top or stay a separate blob.

caption: A child paints a stripe of blue over a dry yellow stripe with translucent watercolour, and the overlap looks green.
expectation: Only the overlapping band is green; the yellow and blue outside the overlap keep their colours.

caption: Sunlight enters a room through a red balloon held up to the window, and a soft red glow falls on the child's hand behind it.
expectation: The glow is on the side away from the window and moves with the balloon; the hand is normal colour when the balloon is lowered.

caption: A cook stirs a spoonful of matcha powder into a glass of milk, and the milk turns pale green.
expectation: Green swirls spread from the spoon and even out; the milk does not return to white.

caption: A concert's lights switch from blue to red, and the white smoke over the stage changes from blue to red at the same instant.
expectation: The smoke shows the colour of whatever light is on it and changes with the lights; unlit smoke is grey.

caption: A woman looks at a rainbow over a field after a shower, and it fades as the rain moves away and the sky clears.
expectation: The rainbow appears opposite the sun, keeps its arc shape while visible, and fades gradually; it does not move across the sky or become brighter as the rain ends.

caption: A woman flips the wall switch in a dark hallway, and the ceiling light comes on.
expectation: The light comes on at the instant the switch moves, not before or after, and stays on; nothing else in the room changes.

caption: A man flips the same wall switch back down, and the ceiling light goes off.
expectation: The light goes out the instant the switch moves and the room falls dark; the light does not fade slowly or flicker back on.

caption: A child pulls the cord on a bedside lamp, and the lamp lights up; she pulls it again and it goes dark.
expectation: Each pull changes the lamp's state at the moment of the click, alternating on and off; the lamp never changes without a pull.

caption: A man presses the button on a flashlight, and the beam comes on; he presses it again and the beam goes out.
expectation: The beam appears and disappears exactly with the clicks; while on, the beam is steady.

caption: A woman points a remote at a television and presses the power button, and the screen lights up.
expectation: The screen comes on a moment after the button press and stays on; it does not light before the press or when the remote points elsewhere.

caption: A driver turns the headlight knob on the dashboard, and the headlights come on and the dashboard dials light up.
expectation: Both the headlights and the dials come on together as the knob turns, and go off together when it is turned back.

caption: A boy unscrews a glowing bulb from a table lamp, and the bulb goes dark as it comes loose.
expectation: The bulb goes out at the moment it loses contact in the socket and stays dark in his hand; it does not keep glowing once removed.

caption: An old bulb in a ceiling fixture flashes bright for an instant and then goes dark for good.
expectation: The flash is brief, the room goes dark right after, and the bulb does not come back on however long one waits; the switch stays where it was.

caption: A man plugs a string of fairy lights into the wall socket, and the whole string lights up along its length.
expectation: All the bulbs come on together the moment the plug goes in; none light before, and none stay dark while the rest glow.

caption: A woman presses the button on an electric kettle, and a small light on the kettle comes on and the switch stays down.
expectation: The indicator lights at the press and stays lit while the switch is down; when the switch pops up later, the light goes out.

caption: A child turns the knob of a night light in a dark bedroom, and the little lamp glows.
expectation: The glow appears when the knob clicks and stays steady; turning the knob back puts it out.

caption: A man switches on a power strip with four lamps plugged into it, and all four lamps come on at once.
expectation: The four lamps light at the same instant as the strip's switch; none lights early or stays off.

caption: A woman presses the power button on a laptop, and the screen lights up and the keyboard glows.
expectation: The screen and keys light shortly after the press; nothing lights before the button is touched.

caption: A boy flicks a light switch up and down several times quickly, and the ceiling light goes on and off in step with each flick.
expectation: Every flick changes the light's state immediately; the light never lags a flick or changes on its own.

caption: A man presses the button on a wall to call an elevator, and the button lights up.
expectation: The button glows from the moment it is pressed and stays lit until the elevator arrives; it does not light before being pressed.

caption: A woman pulls the chain on a ceiling fan light, and the light above the fan comes on while the blades stay still.
expectation: Only the light responds to that chain; the blades do not start turning; a second chain would be needed for the fan.

caption: A man switches on a hairdryer, and it roars and blows hot air; he switches it off and it winds down.
expectation: The airflow starts with the switch and stops within a second of it being turned off; the dryer does not run with the switch off.

caption: A child presses the button on an electric toothbrush, and the head starts buzzing and vibrating.
expectation: The vibration starts at the press and stops at the next press; the brush does not vibrate on its own.

caption: A woman presses the button on a garage door opener, and the garage light comes on and the door begins to rise.
expectation: The light and the door motor respond together right after the press; the door does not move before the button is pressed.

caption: A man plugs in and switches on a neon shop sign, and the tubes flicker and then glow steadily.
expectation: The glow appears only after the switch and settles to a steady light; when switched off the tubes go dark at once.

caption: A woman taps the top of a touch-sensitive lamp, and it lights up; she taps again and it goes off.
expectation: The lamp changes state at each touch and only at a touch; it does not change while her hand is away.

caption: A boy turns on a remote-controlled toy car with the switch on its underside, and its headlights light up and it responds to the controller.
expectation: The lights come on with the switch and the car moves only when the controller is used; it does not move or light while switched off.

caption: A woman opens a microwave door, and the light inside the microwave comes on.
expectation: The interior lights as the door opens and goes dark when it shuts; the turntable does not turn while the door is open.

caption: A man presses the start button on a blender, and the blades spin and the contents whirl; he presses stop and the blades come to rest.
expectation: The blades spin only between the two presses, winding down within a second or two of stop; the contents settle after the blades stop.

caption: A woman turns the knob of a desk fan from off to high, and the blades spin up to speed; she turns it back to off and they slow and stop.
expectation: The blades speed up as the knob is turned up and coast to a stop after it is turned off; they do not spin with the knob at off.

caption: A traffic light at a quiet crossing changes from red to green, and the red lamp goes dark as the green lamp lights.
expectation: Only one lamp is lit at a time and the change is instantaneous; the amber lamp does not light at the same time as green.

caption: A man switches on a string of Christmas lights wound around a tree, and the tree lights up from the plug to the top all at once.
expectation: Every bulb comes on together at the switch; none stays dark or comes on later; the lights do not brighten gradually.

caption: A cyclist presses the button on her bike's rear light, and it begins to blink red.
expectation: The blinking starts at the press and continues at a steady rhythm; another press stops it.

caption: A worker presses the green start button on a conveyor belt, and the belt begins to move; he presses the red button and it stops.
expectation: The belt moves only between the two presses and stops within a moment of the red button; it does not move on its own.

caption: A woman turns the key in a car's ignition, and the dashboard lights up before the engine starts.
expectation: The dashboard lights come on with the key turn; they do not light with the key out or before it is turned.

caption: A boy switches on a battery-powered lantern in a tent, and the tent lights up; he switches it off and the tent goes dark.
expectation: The light responds instantly to the switch each way and stays steady while on.

caption: A man presses the doorbell button beside a front door, and a small light in the doorbell button glows while he presses.
expectation: The glow appears only while the button is pressed and goes out when released.

caption: A woman turns the dial on an electric stove burner, and the coil begins to glow red; she turns it off and the glow fades.
expectation: The glow builds gradually after the dial is turned and fades gradually after it is turned off; the coil does not glow with the dial at off.

caption: A child presses the power button on a handheld game console, and the screen lights up with the start logo.
expectation: The screen lights only after the press and stays on; it does not display anything before.

caption: A man flips the switch on a wall-mounted heater, and its indicator light comes on and its fan starts.
expectation: The light and fan start together with the switch; both stop when it is switched off.

caption: A woman claps her hands twice in a room with a clap-activated lamp, and the lamp comes on.
expectation: The lamp lights right after the second clap and not before; it stays on until the next double clap.

caption: A man switches on a fluorescent tube in a garage, and it blinks a few times before staying lit.
expectation: The blinking begins only after the switch and ends in a steady light; the tube does not light before the switch.

caption: A child presses a button on a toy piano, and the key lights up and the toy's speaker cone can be seen vibrating.
expectation: The key lights while pressed and goes dark when released; nothing lights or vibrates before the press.

caption: A woman presses the wall button for an outdoor floodlight, and the yard lights up.
expectation: The floodlight comes on at the press and lights the yard; pressing again turns it off and the yard goes dark.

caption: A man turns on a shop's escalator with a key switch, and the steps begin to move upward.
expectation: The steps start moving only after the key is turned and run steadily; they stop when the key is turned back.

caption: A woman presses the button on a coffee machine, and a light comes on and coffee begins to drip into the cup.
expectation: The indicator lights with the press and the dripping begins shortly after; nothing happens before the button.

caption: A boy switches off the lamp beside his bed, and only the glow of his alarm clock remains in the room.
expectation: The lamp goes out at the switch and the clock's display stays lit because it is on a different supply; nothing else in the room turns off.

caption: A woman pulls the plug of a running table lamp out of the wall socket, and the lamp goes out.
expectation: The lamp goes dark the instant the plug leaves the socket and stays dark; the switch on the lamp is still on.

caption: A man plugs a desk fan into a socket with its switch already on, and the blades start turning.
expectation: The blades begin to spin when the plug goes in and speed up to a steady rate; they do not spin before the plug is inserted.

caption: A child pulls the plug of a television while a programme is playing, and the screen goes black.
expectation: The picture and sound stop at once when the plug comes out and the screen stays dark; the standby light goes off too.

caption: A boy takes the batteries out of a toy robot that is walking, and the robot stops mid-step.
expectation: The robot's motion and lights stop the moment the batteries come out; it does not finish the step or move again until batteries are replaced.

caption: A woman plugs a charging cable into her phone, and a charging symbol appears on the screen.
expectation: The symbol appears right after the plug clicks in and disappears when it is pulled out; it does not appear before connection.

caption: A man trips over an extension cord and pulls it out of the wall, and the lamp, radio and heater plugged into it all go off together.
expectation: All three devices stop at the same instant the cord comes out; none keeps running.

caption: A girl slides two batteries into a flashlight and screws the cap back on, and when she presses the switch the light comes on.
expectation: The light works only once the batteries are in and the switch is pressed; with the cap off or batteries out it stays dark.

caption: A driver turns the key of a car with a dead battery, and the dashboard stays dark and nothing happens.
expectation: No lights come on and the engine does not turn over; the car does not start on its own.

caption: A woman plugs a charging cable into an electric car, and a light on the charging port comes on.
expectation: The port light comes on after the cable clicks in and goes off when it is removed; it does not light before connection.

caption: A man is using a running hairdryer when its cord is pulled out of the socket, and the dryer falls silent and stops blowing.
expectation: The airflow and noise stop within a second of the plug coming out even though the switch is still on.

caption: A cook plugs in a blender and presses the button, and the blades spin; she unplugs it and the blades slow and stop.
expectation: The blades spin only while the blender is plugged in and the button held; they coast briefly to a stop when unplugged.

caption: A woman vacuums a hallway and the vacuum's cord is yanked from the socket by the doorframe, and the vacuum stops.
expectation: The motor winds down within a second or two of the plug coming out and the machine is silent; it does not restart until plugged in.

caption: A boy swaps a flat battery pack in a remote-control car for a charged one, and the car's lights come on and it drives.
expectation: The car is dead with the flat pack and works only after the charged pack is clipped in; it does not move before.

caption: A woman connects a power bank to her phone, and a light on the power bank comes on and the phone shows it is charging.
expectation: Both indicators appear after the cable is connected and disappear when it is removed.

caption: Dusk falls on a garden, and the solar garden lights along the path come on one by one.
expectation: The lights come on as the sky darkens and stay lit; they do not come on in full daylight.

caption: A camper starts a portable generator, and the string of lights connected to it comes on.
expectation: The lights come on once the generator is running and go out when it is switched off; they do not light while the generator is silent.

caption: A man unplugs a string of fairy lights from the wall, and the whole string goes dark.
expectation: Every bulb goes out at the same instant the plug is pulled; none stays lit.

caption: A woman removes the battery from an e-bike, and the display on the handlebars goes dark.
expectation: The display goes off when the battery is unlatched and comes back when it is clicked in again.

caption: A child places a toy train on its track and switches on the track's power pack, and the train begins to run.
expectation: The train moves only after the power pack is switched on and stops when it is switched off; it does not run on unpowered track.

caption: A man unplugs a glowing electric heater, and the orange glow of its elements fades to dark.
expectation: The fan stops at once and the glow fades gradually over a few seconds; the elements do not glow brighter after unplugging.

caption: A woman unplugs a toaster while its coils are glowing, and the coils fade and the lever pops up.
expectation: The glow dies down after the plug is pulled and the bread stays in until the lever releases; the coils do not keep glowing.

caption: A girl slides the switch on a battery pack attached to a garland of lights, and the garland lights up.
expectation: All the bulbs come on together at the switch; the garland goes dark when the switch is slid back.

caption: A carpenter clips a battery pack into a cordless drill and pulls the trigger, and the drill bit spins.
expectation: The bit spins only with the battery in and the trigger pulled; with the pack removed the trigger does nothing.

caption: A robot vacuum finishes cleaning and drives onto its charging dock, and a charging light on the dock comes on.
expectation: The light comes on once the robot is seated on the dock's contacts and stays on; it is off while the robot is away.

caption: A woman lifts an electric kettle off its base while it is boiling, and the kettle's light goes off and the boiling quiets.
expectation: The light goes out as the kettle leaves the base; the boiling dies down over a few seconds; it resumes only if replaced and switched on.

caption: A photographer's camera screen goes dark mid-shot as the battery runs out, and the camera will not turn back on.
expectation: The screen and lights go off and stay off despite button presses; the camera does not revive until a charged battery is inserted.

caption: A man unplugs a digital alarm clock to move it, and its glowing display goes blank.
expectation: The display goes dark the instant the plug is pulled and lights again, blinking, when plugged in elsewhere.

caption: A woman plugs a laptop charger into the wall and then into the laptop, and the small light on the charger connector comes on.
expectation: The connector light comes on only once both ends are plugged in and goes off when either is removed.

caption: A child presses the accelerator of an electric ride-on car with a flat battery, and the car does not move.
expectation: The car stays still and its lights stay dark no matter how the pedal is pressed; it does not roll on its own.

caption: A man plugs a lamp into a socket and switches on the socket at the wall, and the lamp lights.
expectation: The lamp lights only when the socket switch is on; with the plug in but the socket off it stays dark.

caption: A teenager plugs headphones into a phone playing music, and the phone's speaker goes quiet while the headphones take over.
expectation: The phone's speaker cone stops moving the moment the plug goes in; the on-screen volume icon changes; the phone keeps playing.

caption: A worker connects jumper cables from a running car to a dead car, and the dead car's dashboard lights come on.
expectation: The lights on the dead car appear only after both clamps are connected; they were off before.

caption: A woman unplugs a running sewing machine, and the needle stops and its work light goes out.
expectation: The needle stops within a stitch and the light goes off at the same time; the foot pedal does nothing afterwards.

caption: A man puts a coin-cell battery into a wristwatch, and the second hand starts to tick.
expectation: The hand begins moving only after the battery is seated; it was still before.

caption: A power cut hits a kitchen, and the fridge hum stops, the oven clock goes blank and the ceiling light goes out all at once.
expectation: Everything electrical in the room stops at the same instant; when power returns the light and clock come back together.

caption: A child plugs a nightlight into a low wall socket, and it begins to glow.
expectation: The glow appears as the prongs go into the socket and stays steady; it goes out when the nightlight is pulled out.

caption: A woman opens the battery door of a TV remote and finds the batteries missing, presses the buttons and the TV does not respond.
expectation: The TV stays as it was no matter how many buttons are pressed; after batteries are put in, the remote works.

caption: A man plugs an aquarium pump into the wall, and bubbles start rising from the air stone in the tank.
expectation: The bubbles begin only after the pump is plugged in and stop when it is unplugged; they rise upward through the water.

caption: A teenager's laptop is unplugged from its charger, and the charging light on it goes off while the screen stays on.
expectation: The charging light goes out with the unplugging but the laptop keeps running on its battery; the screen does not go dark.

caption: A woman plugs an electric blanket in and switches it on, and its small control light comes on.
expectation: The light comes on after both the plug and the switch and goes off when either is undone.

caption: A boy's electric scooter slows and stops as its battery runs flat, and its display goes dark.
expectation: The scooter loses power gradually and stops; the display goes off; pressing the throttle does nothing afterward.

caption: A man wheels an electric lawnmower out of range and its cord pulls out of the socket, and the mower stops.
expectation: The blades and motor stop within a second or two of the plug coming out; the mower does not keep cutting.

caption: A storm rolls over a farm at night, and a bolt of lightning flashes from the clouds to the ground, lighting up the fields for an instant.
expectation: The bolt is a jagged bright line from cloud to ground that appears and vanishes within a fraction of a second; the fields are lit only during the flash and are dark again afterwards.

caption: Lightning flashes inside a bank of dark clouds over a city, and the clouds glow for a moment and then go dark.
expectation: The glow is brief and comes from within the clouds; the sky returns to dark right after; the city lights are unaffected.

caption: A family sits in a living room during a storm, and a flash of lightning through the window lights the whole room for an instant.
expectation: The room brightens sharply from the window side and returns to its lamp-lit state immediately; sharp window-frame shadows appear only during the flash.

caption: Lightning strikes a tall tree in a field, and the tree is lit brilliantly for a moment and then smoke rises from its top.
expectation: The bolt ends at the tree, the flash is instantaneous, and the smoke appears after the flash and rises; the tree does not glow afterwards.

caption: Lightning flashes far beyond a mountain range at night, and the outline of the peaks stands out against the lit sky for an instant.
expectation: The sky behind the mountains brightens briefly and the peaks appear as dark shapes; the light is gone in a fraction of a second.

caption: A lightning bolt strikes the sea beyond a beach at night, and the water and the wet sand flash bright and then go dark.
expectation: The bolt descends to the water, the flash reflects in the wet sand and sea surface, and everything returns to dark at once.

caption: Several flashes of lightning light up a stormy sky over a highway one after another, each one lighting the wet road for an instant.
expectation: Each flash is separate and brief with darkness between; the road reflects each flash; the flashes do not merge into a steady glow.

caption: A couple sits in a parked car in a rainstorm, and a lightning flash lights the inside of the car through the rain-streaked windows.
expectation: The interior brightens for an instant from the window side, the raindrops on the glass glint, and the cabin is dim again right after.

caption: Lightning flashes over a wet city street at night, and the flash is mirrored in the puddles and the wet pavement.
expectation: The reflections appear and vanish with the flash and lie below the sky in the water; the streetlights keep their steady glow.

caption: Two children at a window count after a lightning flash, and then flinch as the thunder arrives.
expectation: The flash comes first and the children react a few seconds later; they do not flinch before or during the flash.

caption: A lightning bolt hits the metal rod on top of a tall building, and the rod and roof flash bright for an instant.
expectation: The bolt ends at the rod, the flash is brief, and the building is unchanged afterwards; the bolt does not linger or move along the roof.

caption: During a storm a lightning flash lights up a farmhouse, and a moment later the house's lights flicker.
expectation: The flicker follows the flash, not the other way round; the lights settle back to steady afterwards.

caption: Heat lightning flickers silently on the horizon beyond a lake on a summer night, lighting the far clouds again and again.
expectation: Each flicker is brief and lights only the distant clouds; the near shore stays dark; the flickers do not merge into steady light.

caption: A jagged lightning bolt descends from a cloud to a hilltop, branching as it comes down.
expectation: The bolt runs from cloud to ground with side branches that end in the air, is brightest along the main channel, and is gone in a fraction of a second.

caption: Lightning jumps between two clouds high over a plain, lighting both from inside, with no bolt reaching the ground.
expectation: The flash is inside and between the clouds and brief; the ground below is lit only by the glow, and nothing on the ground is struck.

caption: A dog lying in a hallway jumps up as a lightning flash lights the windows and the house shakes with thunder.
expectation: The flash comes first and the dog reacts after; the light is gone almost immediately.

caption: Lightning strikes a dry hillside, and after the flash a small patch of grass smoulders and smokes.
expectation: The smoke appears at the strike point after the flash and rises; the flash itself is instantaneous and the bolt does not remain.

caption: An airliner flying through a storm cloud is hit by lightning, and a flash runs along its wing before the plane flies on.
expectation: The flash is brief and the plane continues on its course unchanged; the flash does not persist on the aircraft.

caption: Lightning flashes behind a city skyline at night, and the towers stand out as dark silhouettes against the bright sky.
expectation: The towers are dark shapes during the flash and their windows keep their own steady lights before and after.

caption: Lightning flashes over a park during heavy rain, and for an instant every falling raindrop is lit against the dark.
expectation: The rain is visible as bright streaks only during the flash and falls downward; the scene is dark again right after.

caption: A storm approaches a campsite, and the lightning flashes come closer together and brighter as it nears.
expectation: Each flash is still brief and separate; the tents are lit more strongly with the nearer flashes; there is no continuous light.

caption: A lightning bolt strikes a lone tree on a golf course, and the tree's trunk splits with a shower of splinters.
expectation: The split happens at the flash and the splinters fall to the ground; the tree does not glow afterward and does not knit back together.

caption: A lightning flash lights a bedroom through the curtains, and the shadow of the window frame appears on the wall for an instant.
expectation: The shadow appears only during the flash on the wall away from the window and disappears with it.

caption: Lightning flashes over a harbour, and the masts of the boats are lit for an instant and their reflections flash in the water.
expectation: The masts and their reflections brighten together and go dark together; the reflections are below the boats in the water.

caption: Lightning strikes a field of wind turbines, and one turbine's blade tip flashes brightly for an instant.
expectation: The bolt ends at the highest point, the flash is brief, and the blades keep turning as before.

caption: A lightning flash over a lake lights up the underside of the storm clouds, showing their shape for an instant.
expectation: The clouds' undersides are lit from within or below for a fraction of a second and are dark grey again right after.

caption: Lightning flashes as a train crosses a bridge at night, and the bridge and the train's windows are lit for a moment.
expectation: The whole scene brightens briefly and then only the train's own lights remain; the flash does not slow or stop the train.

caption: A bolt of lightning strikes the ground in a desert, and a puff of dust rises from the spot after the flash.
expectation: The bolt comes down to the ground, the dust rises after the flash, and there is no glow left on the sand.

caption: Lightning flashes behind a lighthouse on a stormy coast, and the lighthouse is silhouetted while its own beam keeps sweeping.
expectation: The flash is instantaneous and does not interrupt the steady rotation of the lighthouse beam.

caption: A flash of lightning during a night football match lights up the whole stadium brighter than the floodlights for an instant.
expectation: The extra brightness comes and goes in a fraction of a second, and the floodlights continue as before.

caption: Lightning flashes above a mountain hut in a snowstorm, and the falling snow is lit brightly for an instant.
expectation: The snowflakes appear as bright specks during the flash and are dim again after; they keep falling.

caption: A lightning bolt forks into two branches before reaching the ground, both branches lighting up together.
expectation: The branches share a single trunk from the cloud, appear simultaneously, and vanish together; they do not appear one after another.

caption: Lightning flashes over a river, and a fisherman on the bank is lit for an instant against the dark water.
expectation: The man and his reflection brighten together for a moment; the scene is dark again immediately.

caption: Lightning strikes a metal fence in a field, and a bright flash runs along the fence line for an instant.
expectation: The flash is brief, the fence remains standing and dark afterwards, and the bolt does not linger.

caption: Lightning flashes as a family watches from their porch, and the children's faces are lit for an instant before they cover their ears.
expectation: The faces brighten only during the flash and the ear-covering comes after, when the thunder is expected.

caption: A distant lightning bolt strikes the sea far out from a cliff, so small in the distance that it is over before the eye can follow it.
expectation: The bolt is a thin bright line from cloud to sea, gone at once; the sea around it is lit only briefly.

caption: Lightning flashes over a suburb at night, and every white house front brightens for an instant.
expectation: All the fronts facing the flash brighten together and return to dark together; the streetlamps stay steady.

caption: A camper in a tent sees the canvas light up from a lightning flash outside, then go dark again.
expectation: The canvas glows for a fraction of a second, brightest on the side toward the flash, and returns to dark.

caption: Lightning strikes a tall crane on a construction site at night, and the crane is outlined in a flash for an instant.
expectation: The bolt ends at the top of the crane, the flash is brief, and the crane stands unchanged afterwards.

caption: Lightning flashes over a wheat field, and the stalks bending in the storm wind are lit for an instant.
expectation: The field brightens briefly and the stalks keep bending with the wind; the light is gone at once.

caption: A lightning flash lights a rain-streaked bus shelter, and the people inside are lit for a moment against the dark street.
expectation: The people brighten for a fraction of a second and the shelter's own light continues unchanged afterward.

caption: A welder touches the rod to a steel beam, and a shower of bright sparks bursts from the joint and falls to the floor.
expectation: Sparks appear only while the rod touches the metal, fly outward and downward, and go dark within a short distance; they do not rise or linger on the floor as lights.

caption: A worker presses a spinning angle grinder against a metal pipe, and a fan of orange sparks streams off the wheel.
expectation: The sparks leave the wheel in the direction it is spinning, curve downward under gravity, and fade; they stop the instant the wheel leaves the metal.

caption: A man yanks the plug of a running heater out of the wall socket, and a small spark snaps at the prongs as they come out.
expectation: The spark is a brief flash at the socket at the instant of disconnection and is gone at once; the heater stops.

caption: A mechanic touches the second jumper-cable clamp to a car battery terminal, and a spark jumps at the contact.
expectation: The spark appears exactly as the clamp meets the terminal and vanishes; there is no spark while the clamp is held away.

caption: A tram passes under a wire on a wet night, and its pole throws off blue-white sparks where it rubs the wire.
expectation: The sparks appear at the contact point and move along with the tram; they flash and die instantly and do not fall as burning drops.

caption: A moth flies into a hanging bug zapper on a porch, and there is a brief crackle and flash at the grid.
expectation: The flash happens at the moment of contact and is over instantly; the grid is dark before and after.

caption: A downed power line lies in a wet street, and it sparks and jumps where its broken end touches the ground.
expectation: Sparks flash at the contact point in bursts and the cable end twitches with each burst; the sparks do not travel down the street.

caption: A cook strikes a flint gas-lighter over a stove burner, and a spark jumps from its tip and the gas ignites.
expectation: The spark is a brief flash at the tip; the flame appears right after it, not before; with no gas the spark alone does not stay lit.

caption: A knife is pressed against a spinning sharpening wheel, and a stream of sparks flies off the blade's edge.
expectation: The sparks fly off tangent to the wheel's motion, arc downward, and go dark; they stop when the blade is lifted.

caption: A frayed lamp cord is bumped, and a spark flashes at the bare spot and the lamp flickers.
expectation: The spark is at the damaged spot only and is over instantly; the flicker coincides with the spark.

caption: Bumper cars race under a metal ceiling grid, and their poles throw small sparks where they scrape along it.
expectation: The sparks appear at the pole tips and move with the cars; each flash is brief; there are no sparks from cars whose poles are not touching.

caption: A subway train pulls out of a station, and a flash of sparks lights the tunnel where its shoe touches the rail.
expectation: The flash is at track level beside the train, brief, and lights the tunnel walls for an instant; it does not remain.

caption: An overloaded power drill is run hard, and small sparks flicker through the vents on its motor housing.
expectation: The sparks are visible only inside the vents while the motor runs and stop when the trigger is released.

caption: A hiker strikes a ferro rod with a striker, and sparks spray onto the tinder below.
expectation: The sparks fly in the direction of the stroke and fall downward onto the tinder, going dark on the way or as they land.

caption: A worker cuts a steel bar with a cut-off saw, and a long plume of sparks shoots out behind the blade and rains onto the floor.
expectation: The plume points away from the direction of cut, the sparks arc down, and they fade before or as they hit the floor.

caption: A bad connection in a fuse box sparks and pops, and the lights in the house go out.
expectation: The spark is brief and at the box; the lights go out immediately after; they do not come back on by themselves.

caption: A blacksmith hammers a red-hot bar on an anvil, and tiny sparks fly off with each blow.
expectation: Sparks appear only at the moment of each strike, scatter outward from the impact, and go dark as they fall.

caption: A boy drags a metal rake along a concrete path in the dark, and faint sparks flick from the tines.
expectation: The sparks appear where the metal scrapes the concrete and stop when the rake is lifted; they die instantly.

caption: A worker touches a live wire to a metal bracket by mistake, and a bright spark flashes and leaves a black mark.
expectation: The flash is instantaneous at the contact point and the dark mark remains afterwards; the wire does not keep glowing.

caption: A car's wheel rim scrapes a curb at night, and a brief spray of sparks flies from the contact.
expectation: The sparks appear only during the scrape, fly backward relative to the car's motion, and fade at once.

caption: A stunt rider drags a metal knee slider along the track in a turn, and sparks trail out behind it.
expectation: The sparks stream backward from the point of contact and die out along the track; they stop when the slider lifts.

caption: A woman plugs a phone charger into a worn socket, and a small spark flashes at the plug as it goes in.
expectation: The spark is a single brief flash at the moment of contact; the charger then works normally.

caption: A grinder is used to sharpen a lawnmower blade, and the sparks pouring off the wheel bounce on the concrete floor before fading.
expectation: The sparks fall in arcs, some skip off the floor, and all go dark within a short distance; none rise.

caption: A locomotive brakes hard into a station, and sparks fly from its wheels where the brakes grip.
expectation: The sparks appear at the wheels only while braking and stream backward and down; they stop as the train stops.

caption: A worker with a plasma cutter slices a steel sheet, and a fountain of sparks pours from the underside of the cut.
expectation: The sparks fall away beneath the sheet along the line of the cut, fading as they drop; they stop when the torch stops.

caption: A child scuffs a toy car with metal wheels across a rough stone slab, and tiny sparks appear under the wheels.
expectation: The sparks appear only where the wheels scrape and while the car moves; they vanish instantly.

caption: A cook flicks a stovetop lighter, and a blue spark jumps between its two metal tips.
expectation: The spark is a brief bridge between the tips at the click and is gone; there is no spark while the button is not pressed.

caption: A metalworker files a piece of steel at a bench, and each stroke throws a few sparks that drop to the bench.
expectation: Sparks appear only during each stroke, fall downward, and go dark before or on landing.

caption: An electrician tests a wire and it shorts against the box, and a flash and puff of smoke come from the spot.
expectation: The flash is instantaneous and the smoke rises after it; the wire does not glow afterward.

caption: A horse's iron shoe strikes a stone on a path in the dusk, and a spark flashes under the hoof.
expectation: The spark appears at the instant of the strike and is gone; there is no spark on soft ground.

caption: A worker drops a steel rod on a concrete floor in a dim workshop, and a spark flicks from the point of impact.
expectation: The spark is a single flash at the moment the rod hits and vanishes; the rod bounces and settles.

caption: A skateboarder grinds a metal rail at night, and sparks trail from the truck along the rail.
expectation: Sparks appear along the contact and stream behind the board; they stop when the board leaves the rail.

caption: A worker starts an arc welder and the arc lights the whole garage in blue-white, throwing hard shadows.
expectation: The intense light appears only while the arc is struck, flickers, and the garage goes back to normal light when it stops.

caption: A street sweeper's steel brush spins against a kerb at night, and a stream of sparks runs along the ground beside the machine.
expectation: The sparks stream in the direction the brush throws them and fade quickly; they follow the machine as it moves.

caption: A man throws a switch on an old-fashioned knife switch panel, and a small arc snaps at the contacts as they close.
expectation: The arc appears at the contacts at the moment of closing and vanishes; the connected lamp comes on.
